incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert at 06:22 UTC — surge of 5xx and connection resets from Private endpoints served out of GCP eu-west3. Multiple healthchecks failing across Interconnect/VPN and VPC-peered customer networks. Ticket auto-created: INC-76248.

maya (oncall-sre): I'm on it. Paging @raj and @emily. Which customers are flagging this?

olivia (solutions-eng): AcmeCorp and BetaCorp reported increased errors and 502s for on-prem integrations. Both have Private deployments hosted with egress through eu-west3.

nathen (cs): CS already messaged both accounts and asked for request IDs + timestamps. Acme sent a trace showing TCP resets from our edge.

emily (infra): I'm seeing BGP withdraws on our VPC peerings to eu-west3. Flap patterns every ~30s. Looks like route withdraws then re-announces.

raj (oncall-sre): Can you dump the peering status and route table?

emily (infra): pasted command output below:

```
$ gcloud compute networks peerings list --project redwood-prod
NAME            NETWORK        STATE
peer-acme       private-net-1  ACTIVE
peer-beta       private-net-2  ACTIVE

$ gcloud compute routes list --filter="network~private-" --project redwood-prod
NAME                  DEST_RANGE      NEXT_HOP
route-peer-acme       10.10.0.0/16     peering:peer-acme
route-peer-beta       10.20.0.0/16     peering:peer-beta
```

But control-plane logs show intermittent route withdraws from peer-acme toward eu-west3: ``BGP: UPDATE withdraw from ASN 64512 for prefix 10.10.0.0/16``

maya (oncall-sre): OK plan: 1) apply temporary per-customer reroute to eu-west1 for affected customers, 2) enable aggressive client-side retries/backoff in proxy, 3) open priority case with GCP and request fabric-level investigation. I'll do 1 and 2 now.

raj (oncall-sre): I'll prepare the traffic-splitting rule. Use the control CLI:

```
# add failover route in Redwood control plane for AcmeCorp -> eu-west1
redwood ctl route override --selector "customer=AcmeCorp" --add-region eu-west1 --priority 1000 --dry-run
redwood ctl route override --selector "customer=AcmeCorp" --add-region eu-west1 --priority 1000 --apply
```

Applying for Acme and Beta now. Will monitor for decreased errors.

olivia (solutions-eng): Posting customer-facing update: "We are experiencing degraded private connectivity for some EU customers using GCP eu-west3. We have temporary reroutes in place and are working with GCP on a fix. No data loss reported; request retries may succeed."

incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to infra-sre team sent to @oncall-sre.

emily (infra): Opened priority-1 case with GCP: CCed peering / networking team. GCP support-bot responded: "We are observing control-plane route instability affecting peering fabric in europe-west3; investigation in progress. Possible route reflector bug. No ETA yet."

gcp-support-bot: Case GCP-2026-004321 created. Current status: Investigating. Logs requested: BGP dumps from our edge and AS path traces.

raj (oncall-sre): After applying overrides, error rate for Acme dropped from 12% to ~1.8% over last 6 minutes. BetaCorp showing similar improvement.

maya (oncall-sre): Good. Notify SRE-hours and prepare for longer window. I'll rotate handoff at 07:00 UTC — @raj you take primary until 10:00.

raj (oncall-sre): Taking primary. I'll keep the overrides in place and watch. If GCP confirms fix, we'll revert and document.

olivia (solutions-eng): CS update to customers posted. Also offered to open direct line between Acme network ops and our infra if they want.

nathen (cs): AcmeOps replied: "Thanks — we've confirmed traffic to eu-west1 is successful and integrations are returning to normal." They asked for a postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

maya (oncall-sre): Action items captured for postmortem: 1) Collect BGP update dumps (emily), 2) Timeline of impact per customer (nathen + olivia), 3) Review Redwood control-plane failover automation and add per-region automatic failover for private peering (engineering), 4) Runbook update for GCP regional fabric incidents.

emily (infra): Dumped BGP update logs and uploaded to INC-76248. Sample snippet:

```
06:21:55 ASN64512 UPDATE: NLRI withdrawn 10.10.0.0/16
06:21:56 ASN64512 ANNOUNCE: 10.10.0.0/16 via gw-1
06:22:26 ASN64512 UPDATE: NLRI withdrawn 10.10.0.0/16
```

maya (oncall-sre): Looks like repeated withdraws. GCP says it's a fabric control-plane reflection problem. We'll leave overrides until GCP confirms global RIB stability for 15m.

olivia (solutions-eng): Posting interim status on status.redwood.ai: "Degraded — Private connectivity for some EU customers using GCP eu-west3. Temporary reroutes applied to eu-west1. Customers may experience intermittent errors. We will update every 30 mins."

incident-bot: Status page update published. Next scheduled update at 06:55 UTC.

raj (oncall-sre): Quick checklist for whoever picks this up later: check `redwood ctl route override --list` to see which selectors are active; confirm revert command: `redwood ctl route override --selector "customer=AcmeCorp" --remove-region eu-west1 --apply` once GCP stable.

maya (oncall-sre): Thanks team. Summary for handoff note to postmortem: suspected cause = GCP fabric BGP route reflection bug in eu-west3 causing intermittent withdraws; mitigation = per-customer control-plane reroute to eu-west1 + client retry/backoff; follow-ups = automate region-failover, improve observability for BGP withdraw patterns, coordinate with GCP for root fix and timeline.

raj (oncall-sre): Leaving detailed timestamps in the ticket. I'm primary until 10:00 UTC. If anything changes, ping here or escalate to PD.

nathen (cs): I'll collate customer impact table and send to accounts.

olivia (solutions-eng): Will prepare customer-facing postmortem draft once we have root-cause confirmation.

incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-76248 — status: Mitigated (temporary reroutes in place).

maya (oncall-sre): Closing active paging. Keep monitoring.
